newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand weathered a roller coaster week to finish a quiet Friday session moderately higher on the day.
The unit was last quoted at 4.4745/4775 against dollar from 4.4820/4840 late Thursday after having touched a 4.4945 bid on Thursday - its weakest level in three months.
Dealers said participants had got overly long U.S. dollars this week on the back of more than $1 billion worth of importer orders for the greenback which played havoc with local forex dealings.
But on Friday, a few of the longs recanted, allowing the rand some breathing space up to an intraday best of 4.4700 over the morning.

"The markets got nervous with the move up in the rand, on the back of a large order, and after that I think the market decided to get itself caught extra long (dollars), but found themselves this morning with no demand for dollars," said one dealer.
Volumes were minimal and the market's skittishness was evident when a $50 million dollar order, relatively small by this week's standards, sent the unit into the red around midday.
The weakness didn't last and the rand marched back into the black over the afternoon after Reserve Bank intervention at the 4.4815 level.
The rand also stabilised in cross rate dealings and was last at 0.3782/3786 marks from 0.3801/3804 Thursday and 7.3231/3325 rand to the British pound from 7.3359/3453 yesterday.
It was down against the yen at 26.8745/9030 from 25.8863/9259 before.
Bond market dealings were comparatively quiet with range trading the order of the day while many players left their desks to work on their handicaps at an Eskom golf tournament.
The R150 long bond was last at 14.89 percent from 14.935 percent Thursday.
Dealers said the local debt market was likely to continue range-trading next week between 14.87-14.97 percent.
"I think it's rangebound and capped at 14.87 really," said one.

Foreigners channelled more money into local debt on Thursday, chalking up net purchases of 400.98 million rand's worth of South African bonds, having bought 173.91 million rand's worth on Wednesday, the Bond Exchange said.
South Africa's m/ney market shortage rose to 7.780 billion rand on Thursday from 7.615 billion rand on Wednesday, the Reserve Bank said.
Domestic money market rates were were unchanged from Thursday with three month NCD rates from major banks at 16.40 percent offered and 90-day BA rates at 14.90 percent.
Nominal Bond Exchange turnover inched up to 7.48 billion rand on Thursday from 7.41 billion rand on Wednesday.
